contracts.title: 4.4 · An installed app checks for a newer published release offered by its own release channel, downloads and verifies it, and installs it only at a quiet moment: not in the first ten minutes after a launch, not while the window has been used or an agent session has worked in the last ten minutes, and never while a library seed or project snapshot is being written. The user can install it from the gear without waiting for a quiet moment, but seeds and snapshots still hold the restart with the window open and the update pending. Installing stops its database and restarts through the platform's installer into the new app using the app's lifecycle handoff.

reported.note: Final pnpm gate passes: installed menu and automatic updates stay pending while snapshots run, including snapshots beginning during the quiet read; retry uses the existing download and restarts once.

contracts.title: 4.5 · A failed release check or download leaves the app running and can be retried; equal and older releases never replace it, concurrent checks share one download, and quitting stops updates.

4.6 · Releases contain only work merged to main and verified on all three systems by main's own CI run of that commit; every later main build has a higher version, and a rerun cannot replace a newer published release. One platform's failure holds only that platform: a release publishes with every platform whose build is complete, and a platform whose build is not keeps its last good build's update feed and installer entry, so an installed app never meets a release that lacks its own platform's feed, and its one-liner installs the last build that has its platform. Every asset is uploaded into the draft before it publishes, and publishing is its last write: a late platform's build waits for the next version; nothing is uploaded to a published release.

4.7 · Check for updates in the gear checks the published releases now, using the same updater as the automatic check. Concurrent requests share the work. If no newer build is needed, the menu says the app is up to date and identifies the running build.

4.8 · The menu shows when a new build is ready or restarting. A ready build restarts the app through the existing lifecycle, waiting with the window open while a seed writes the library or a start-up or daily project snapshot is being written, including when the user asks from the menu; waiting neither downloads the ready build again nor starts a second restart.

reported.note: Final pnpm gate passes: startup and daily snapshots hold automatic and menu main updates with the old window open, then reuse the ready build for one restart.

contracts.title: 4.9 · A failed manual update check or download shows its reason, leaves the running app alone, and can be retried from the gear.

4.10 · In a copy that does not install releases (a development checkout, a portable build), Check for updates explains that it does not update itself; the request neither fetches a build nor restarts the app.

4.12 · A named acceptance run can hold automatic release installation until it releases its hold or a finite ceiling expires; overlapping runs keep independent holds. Downloads continue, and an explicit Restart to update still installs once no seed or project snapshot is being written.

4.13 · The user chooses when a downloaded release may install itself: whenever quiet (the default), only inside their daily quiet hours, or never on its own (manual only); the quiet-moment rule still applies inside the hours, and their own Restart to update installs in every mode once no seed or project snapshot is being written.

4.29 · A failed read or change in the gear's Updates section is written to the console (so app.log) and shown: Update channel, When updates install and Open at sign-in show a failed first read, unchangeable, instead of vanishing, and a hidden switch or error line is never displayed

capabilities.title: 4 · Drill-down
capabilities.description: Clicking a story node opens a panel that explains the story in plain words: its sentences, and its capability tree, each capability pointing at the ones it builds on, including any in other stories, named with their story. The tree has a space of its own inside the panel, where the user drags it around and zooms it; it opens zoomed out to fit the whole tree, as far as the least zoom allows, and an icon in that space's corner opens the same tree in a larger window over the forest, which opens fitted too. Each capability's card says proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested on a strip coloured as 0.2 coloured those words, with the agent's report and storytree's as labelled marks (ADR-0743, ADR-0744). Clicking one of the story's own capabilities, in the panel's tree or in the larger window, shows it below the panel's tree: its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts on request (ADR-0659).

contracts.title: 4.1 · A story whose third capability builds on the first two gives its sentences, its capabilities in build order each with its sentences and its health as the agent reports it, and a diagram with exactly two arrows.
4.2 · A capability that builds on a capability in another story shows an arrow to it, named with that story, and that capability's card says its word.
4.3 · A capability with no description says "no description yet" instead of leaving a blank.
4.4 · A contract the agent reported red, then green, shows "red, then green"; one reported only green says so.
4.5 · Storytree's own column shows beside the agent's report only where something wrote it.

4.6 · The panel shows the story's sentences and its diagram, and below the diagram only the capability selected: its word, its sentences, its health as the agent reports it, and its contracts folded until asked for. No front cover shows in it.
4.7 · When a story opens, the capability shown is the first in build order that has not landed, or the first if all have; one clicked stays shown, and a choice outside the story falls back.

4.8 · Each of the story's capabilities is a card you can click, marked when selected and tinted by its word (a healthy card edged green, an unhealthy one red), never by the agent's report; another story's capability is in the tree but cannot be clicked.

4.9 · The capability tree is a graph of fixed-size cards: each capability sits above the ones it builds on, and another story's capability sits one row below the capability that builds on it, not in one row with every other outside capability.

4.10 · Each card, another story's too, has a strip across its top saying its word, proposed, healthy, unhealthy or untested (ADR-0744), coloured as 0.2 coloured it (proposed amber, healthy green, unhealthy red, untested grey), and the agent's report and storytree's as marks labelled "the agent reports" and "storytree saw", storytree's only where something wrote it. The work state (planned, in progress, landed) is not on the card.

4.11 · The capability tree has its own space inside the panel, moved by dragging and zooming, with no scroll bars and never out of reach. It, and the larger window, open with the whole tree fitted in the frame and centred, never above full size nor below the least zoom; the larger window's "Fit" puts that view back. An icon in the panel space's corner, labelled "Open in a larger window", opens the larger window.

4.12 · The capability selected, when it is not healthy, says why under its word and who moves it (the agent, or you), naming the contracts that carry it; a contract whose last verdict was not re-run says "last seen failing <date>, not re-run since"; a healthy one says nothing more.

4.13 · In a project whose health nothing verifies, a built capability's card and detail lead with what the agent reports, labelled as the agent's, and say storytree does not check this project's tests yet, never untested or who moves it
4.14 · A parked capability's card keeps its word and reason and says it is parked, naming the arc
4.15 · A mapped story's panel says it is mapped: here before storytree, assumed to be working, with its file and line counts, and shows no health

4.16 · Opening a story's island, the smallest, the largest or the library's, answers within 100 ms with no frame over 50 ms, and its panel is open within 1 s or shows progress; closing the panel likewise (verified by the Mint box's lag run)

contracts.title: 4.36 · A selected story's panel shows a minimal risk bar: its rating out of ten, the users it could reach and its extra checks with what sets each off, no graph

4.37 · Wherever storytree's verified colour shows, on a capability's card and detail and on each contract, it says its source: verified locally, from CI, or locally and from CI; a reason not green names the source of the contracts carrying it; an entry with no source recorded says none

capabilities.title: 5 · Agent capability claims
capabilities.description: Shows on the world what each running session holds. Each capability claimed by a session that has a row in the running-sessions list (capability 7) carries one flag in that session's colour, standing inside the capability's territory (ADR-0968, which replaced the inset border band of ADR-0923 D1 and the outline of ADR-0825 D3). Each session has its own stable colour, the same on its flags and on its row, never the proven green or the needs-you amber. The flag keeps its size on screen and becomes a dot on an island too small to carry a pennant; it drops in with one ring at its foot when the claim arrives, stands still while held, furls and greys when its holder goes quiet, and lifts away when the claim is released or lands, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no surveyed code the claimed capability's equal share is marked as a staked lot, a dashed white line inside its border; a capability with no code on an island that has code draws nothing. No band, outline, fill or coast tint is drawn for a claim, so a territory's fill stays health's. A flag carries no visible agent name, reason text or hooks warning. It follows the agent link's claims and sessions, so a holder whose hooks have reported goes quiet after the quiet time; a holder whose hooks have never reported is never quiet as idle. Subagents and supervised lanes folded under a parent flag in the parent's colour, a session with no row flags nothing, and an increment claim draws nothing on the world (ADR-0923 D2). A growth replay flags the capabilities its recorded sessions held as it reaches them (contract 5.7). Missing hooks are reported by the agent link's setup check (capability 8, contract 8.5). *History: the wisps of ADR-0736 were removed by ADR-0804 D9; ADR-0825 D3 outlined a claimed territory and tinted the coast; ADR-0923 dropped the coast tint; ADR-0968 (2026-10-10) made the mark a flag and added lots.*

contracts.title: 5.1 · Session A claims "email form", and a flag in A's colour stands on that capability's territory, with no visible agent name or reason text; A's claim on a capability on a second island is flagged there too. An increment claim flags nothing, whatever its touches name (ADR-0968 D1, ADR-0923 D2).
5.2 · For a holder whose hooks have reported, after the quiet time with no new line its flags furl and grey; when A reports the capability landed, its flag lifts away.
5.3 · A session seen only through its tool calls keeps its flags unfurled even past the quiet time; the map draws no hooks warning.
5.4 · None of this changes how a capability's state is drawn.

5.5 · A session's colour is the same on every read, on its flags and on its row in the sessions list, and is never the proven-green colour. A subagent folded under its parent flags its claims in its parent's colour, and a session with no row flags nothing.

5.6 · A capability a running session claims carries one flag in that session's colour, standing in its territory at a constant size on screen, a pennant on its pole however far out the globe is zoomed and never a dot (ADR-1039); it drops in with one ring at its foot, stands still while held, furls and greys when the session is quiet, and lifts away when the claim goes, with no movement under reduced motion. On an island with no code the claimed share is marked as a lot. The flag is the only claim mark: no band, outline or fill, and no coast tint (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D1, narrowing ADR-0804 D9)

5.7 · Replaying a growth, the sessions recorded with the latest stage the replay has reached flag the territories they held, each flag arriving as the replay reaches it, none before the first (ADR-0968, ADR-0923 D3)

capabilities.title: 7 · Running sessions
capabilities.description: A see-through strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width and collapsible by its header (contract 7.17) lists one plain row per session that has not ended, claimed or not (ADR-0749 D1; ADR-0737 D1's removal of off-plan rows and their evidence stands, and capability 6 stays retired), showing facts as labels and no prose on the owner's behalf: anything that needs the owner is an open question on the arc surface (ADR-0824). An unclaimed row is named from its harness and what it works in; a session working in several worktrees says so (D2). Each row shows what it is doing, its context bar and its available context total. Explicitly related subagents and supervised lanes fold beneath their parent behind “+N”. Each row has one expander (the same control as “+N”), closed at first; expanded, it lists each worktree the session works in (full path on hover) labelled unmerged or merged, the commands it started and has not seen finish, and the files in its window, read from the agent link's window reading (9.10) only when expanded, then its children. No row uses a state colour; each root row wears its session’s own colour, the colour of its wisps on the forest (capability 5, ADR-0736), and a hovered wisp highlights its row. Hovering or focusing a row lights its claimed islands and dims the others. Waiting rows stay plain, working and waiting read from each session's turns (ADR-0754 D5); rows neither working nor waiting are idle by their state alone, and are listed first under the strip's History tab rather than on Live, which a search box narrows (ADR-1002 D4); ended sessions are hidden. Parent relationships and totals are read only when recorded or supplied by the agent link; missing values are not guessed. *Narrowed in place, 2026-10-05 (ADR-0804 D9, decision_5aadb523c1cb; ADR-0923 D2, decision_027f3b08bb8b): no wisps are drawn, so a row's colour is the colour of its traversal and of its claimed territories' outlines, and the hovered-wisp clause no longer applies. Hovering or focusing a row lights only the islands holding capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (contract 7.4).*

contracts.title: 7.1 · The list includes once each session the agent-link reading lists (agent link 4.9, 4.12), whether or not it holds a claim: a session holding unmerged work stays even after it ended, while a verified close-out, or an ended or quiet session with no open work past the user's leave-after setting (1 hour by default, read as idle-after is), is excluded (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0758 D3, D5, narrowing ADR-0749 D1 and ADR-0737 D1). Sessions at work come first and the rest fold into the idle row (7.10). A waiting row stays plain; working and waiting come from the session's turns (agent link 4.8), and only a session whose hooks report no turns is judged by the user's idle-after setting. A row's task uses its claim reason or held increment title; a session with neither is named from its harness and what it works in (its latest claim's branch, else its last folder), held to 40 characters, and never labelled off plan. A session whose lines name more than one folder shows how many worktrees it works in, naming them on hover (D2).

7.2 · An explicit parent relation or subagent-started record folds that child under its parent behind the row's “+N” expander (7.8), closed at first as every row is (7.8); expanding reveals its task and collapsing hides it again. No child is duplicated at the top. A recorded subagent lacking its own session reading is shown as observed, without inventing a live state; absent parent relations are never inferred from claim wording.

7.4 · Hovering or keyboard-focusing a row lights the forest islands containing the capabilities it, or a subagent folded under it, claimed, and dims the other islands; an increment it holds lights none, whatever its touches name (ADR-0923 D2). Leaving the row restores the ordinary forest appearance. With no claimed capability the row does not arbitrarily select one.

7.5 · Every row reserves an empty context-bar slot. When an agent-link context total is supplied the row displays that total; when absent it displays an unavailable mark, never zero. This increment draws no composition segments, thresholds or estimated totals.

7.6 · Each row's bar is its session's tokens used (agent link 9.5), read again every 10 seconds, on one scale for every row: 1,000,000 tokens across the full width (the display's choice; a reading has no window size, ADR-0728). A Claude Code reading's bar is split into Injected, Grounding, Implementation and Other in proportion to its composition (9.8), and hovering gives the tokens and each group's estimated share; a Claude Code row marks its reading's context guidance (the user's setting, 600,000 by default; ADR-0739 D1), one mark; a row whose reading carries no guidance has none; a Codex row is one raw segment with no marks. With 400,000 tokens split 2:2:3:1, the segments are 10%, 10%, 15% and 5% wide. The list's header names the four groups in bar order, each beside a swatch in its segment's colour.

7.7 · The list hands the knowledge core its rows as the core's roster, each row with its children in the row's colour. Clicking a row selects its session in the core and marks the row (a child's row selects its parent); clicking the selected row again clears the selection, and the core then shows no session's traversal. The list and the core share one selection (ADR-0738 D5, ADR-0921).

7.8 · Every row has one expander, an arrow at the row's start, closed at first, opening only when the user expands it; a row with children counts them as “+N” after its name (7.2's control, not a second one). Expanded, a row lists, under a small “Worktrees” label, every worktree it works in, oldest first, each by its folder's own name with its full path on hover and its merge label (7.15); then its “Running” block (7.16); then, under a small “Files” label, the files in its window (agent link 9.10), each once, in the order first opened, with files no longer in the window muted; then its children. Files are read from the agent link's window reading only when a row is expanded, never from a second reader; a session without a window reading says why and lists no files. Collapsing hides the detail and the children again.

7.9 · The running-sessions list shows facts as labels and prints no prose about a session: no 'needs you' chip or line, no close-out why, no 'holding unmerged' line. A row is idle, listed under History rather than Live and not counted in the header, by its state alone (working, or waiting within the idle-after time). Owner decisions surface only as open questions on the arc surface (ADR-0824 D1, D2, narrowing ADR-0758 D1; ADR-1002 D4).

7.10 · The Live tab lists only the sessions at work (working, or waiting within the idle-after time); listed sessions that are neither are not on it, and no "N idle" row stands for them. The header's count is unchanged. With idle sessions listed and none at work, the tab says "No sessions at work" and, as a button that opens History, how many are idle there; with none listed it says "No running sessions" (ADR-1002 D4, narrowing ADR-0758 D5; ADR-0824).

7.11 · A session whose close-out is unverified (a no, or a yes the facts disagree with) stays listed, and its row folds and counts by its state alone, showing neither a mark nor a reason for its close-out (agent link 4.12; ADR-0758 D3 as narrowed by ADR-0824 D1).

7.12 · A session holding unmerged work (agent link 4.9's open work) stays listed, even after it ended, wherever its row sits; its row prints no line about it, the fact showing only as its worktrees' "unmerged" labels (7.15) (ADR-0754 D4, ADR-0824 D2).

7.13 · When the listed sessions run on more than one machine, each row names the machine its session runs on (the latest its activity lines name), beside its name; when they all run on one machine, no row names one.

7.14 · A row whose session holds no claim is named by its app's title (agent link 4.19), held to the label limit, before falling back to its harness and place. Expanding any row opens with up to three lines describing it, from recorded words only: the app's title where the row's name is not it, the objective of the increment it holds, and the app's latest status. A row with none of these shows no description.

7.15 · Each worktree in a row's detail carries one short label from the branches its session recorded there: "merged" when none still holds open work; for an open branch with a pull request, "PR #n" and what it waits on (in merge queue, draft, failing, or in CI while its checks run), or "PR #n" alone when its checks pass or it has none; "unmerged" when no open branch there has a pull request read. The main line, or no branch, carries no label; a branch recorded with no folder is folded under the folder last worked in, and none is dropped.

7.16 · An expanded row's Running block lists the commands its session started and has not seen finish, background ones included, each by its first words (one line, ellipsised, full command on hover) and how long it has run.

7.17 · The list is a strip along the forest pane's bottom, spanning its width (up to 40% of the pane tall, scrolling vertically inside, never horizontally), see-through so the globe shows behind it. Its header (name, count, colour legend and a caret) hides and expands the whole list like the arcs bar's handle: it starts expanded, collapsed leaves only the header, and the choice is kept per project in the page's storage (a missing or foreign value reads as expanded). While the strip is open its header also carries a size control beside the caret, reading Expand or Restore for what a press gives and working from the keyboard: expanded, the strip (Live or History) fills the forest pane from top to bottom, covering the globe and its controls until restored, its rows still scrolling inside; the size is kept per project in the page's storage (a missing or foreign value reads as the usual height), and collapsing then opening the strip returns the kept size. Every row starts collapsed and its expander opens it (7.8), with no expand-all control; an expanded row lays its Worktrees, Running and Files side by side, in one column when narrow. At either size the strip keeps clear of an open story panel and of the stale-forest mark, and an open Arcs drawer lies over it.
