capabilities.title: 5 · Send feedback
capabilities.description:
A button in the app lets the user describe a problem or suggestion and opens it as a draft GitHub issue on storytree's repository. They see what they are sending and submit it themselves.

As built: Help → Send feedback provides editable title and message fields and an explicit Open GitHub draft action. The package constructs https://github.com/storytree-ai/storytree/issues/new with only those two user-authored fields; the desktop carries the OS external-browser action. It attaches no project contents, paths, transcripts or logs. A failed handoff preserves the message and offers retry or copy, with an explicit copy failure and selectable original text. Success says “Opened a draft”, leaving GitHub submission to the user. Closing help sends nothing.

Evidence: packages/app-setup/evidence/help/README.md. Fake-opener tests and the actual desktop renderer cover no-project and both-forest access, cancellation, editing, retry, copy, exact payloads and honest success status. No issue was submitted by the checks.

2026-10-06 foundation: the view additionally accepts an optional feedbackIdentity bridge. Only entering Send feedback queries its status. Sign-in remains optional, and a separate Add account to message action inserts the verified email and portable Storytree ID into the editable message, which the user may remove before copy or browser handoff. No bridge is wired into the shipped desktop yet; that integration is parked on the identity arc. Local contract 5.5 and Chromium fixture captures: packages/app-setup/evidence/identity/README.md. These are not live provider or deployed desktop acceptance.

capabilities.title: 14 · PostHog delivery
capabilities.description: Deliver sanitized milestones through the Node client to PostHog US (ADR-0908) with a small durable offline queue and bounded CLI shutdown.

contracts.title: 14.1 · A consented milestone survives offline failure and process restart in a bounded disk queue; a successful retry removes only the delivered entries.
14.2 · Delivery uses PostHog US (ADR-0908) through the Node transport with IP/GeoIP collection disabled and no added person properties; missing configuration performs no network request.
14.3 · Turning sharing off clears queued milestones and blocks subsequent network requests, including another client's pending flush; CLI shutdown awaits a bounded flush.

14.4 · A shipped build is stamped at build time with only PostHog's public project token, which makes sharing available with its retention and deletion contact; a private key refuses the build, and an unstamped copy offers no sharing.

capabilities.title: 11 · Pipeline wiring
capabilities.description: At setup, or when a project adopts a pipeline, the agent wires the project's tests, and the jobs the parts it has on contribute (Guardrails' storytree check), into the user's CI through `wire_pipeline`, and proposes branch protection for the user to approve.

contracts.title: 11.1 · In a GitHub project, `wire_pipeline` writes storytree's workflow: on every pull request and push to main it runs the project's install and test commands on each system the user chose, and storytree check from storytree's source pinned to the user's storytree release
11.2 · In a project not on GitHub, `wire_pipeline` writes nothing and answers with the commands to add to the pipeline the user has
11.3 · `wire_pipeline` proposes branch protection (merge only what CI verified) as a command for the user to approve, and never changes a repository setting itself

11.5 · When GitHub refuses protection on the repository's plan (a free private repository), wire_pipeline offers merging only after every check passes instead of a command that would fail, and only reads the setting

11.6 · In a project that imports a folder recorded by repository and commit, `wire_pipeline`'s pipeline fetches it at that commit into the place beside the checkout where the folder sits, and installs its own dependencies, before the project's install and tests
11.7 · An import recorded with no repository is named by `wire_pipeline` as one CI cannot fetch, with what the user can do about it
11.8 · A contributed job that asks for the history (storytree check) is checked out with origin/main, so the self-equal assertion check compares the change with it

11.9 · wire_pipeline writes, lists and proposes as status checks only the jobs the parts the host mounts contribute: with Guardrails switched off its pipeline has no storytree check job and its branch protection names no storytree check status

11.10 · The workflow wire_pipeline writes runs with read-only repository permissions, keeps no checkout credentials, uses every action at a pinned commit, and takes storytree's source at the full commit of the user's release

capabilities.title: 6 · Make a folder a project
capabilities.description: After the user says yes, a folder becomes a storytree project: the one check that refuses a folder already part of a project or a second trunk, the project opened (and its library seeded with the starter pack the first time), the folder recorded and approved as this machine's trunk, the marker left, and the app's choice recorded. Joining an existing project from another machine's checkout is the same step on purpose. Reading which project a folder belongs to stays with the hooks, in project routing.

contracts.title: 6.1 · A project name the library would refuse is refused when setting a folder up, and nothing is written.

6.2 · A folder that is a project's trunk, is inside one, is a git worktree of one, or holds one is refused when set up as another project, even with its marker gone, and nothing is written (ADR-0757 D3).
6.3 · A second folder for a project that already has a trunk on this machine is refused, joining or not, saying to work in a git worktree of the trunk; the trunk keeps routing (ADR-0757 D1, D3).

6.4 · A new folder given an existing project's name is refused unless it joins on purpose, on any machine, and the refusal suggests the first name no project has (name-2, name-3…); a matching folder name never joins (ADR-0757 D3, D4).

6.5 · A machine with no trunk for an existing project adds its checkout only on purpose (join), after which a git worktree of that checkout routes to the project, one project shared by both machines; joining a project that does not exist is refused (ADR-0757 D2, D4).

6.6 · A trunk whose folder is gone from this machine (moved or deleted) is forgotten when the project is set up or joined; a moved folder is never adopted on sight and reaches its project only once joined on purpose (ADR-0942 D4). A folder still there keeps its trunk, marker or not (6.2).

6.7 · Setting a new project up gives its factory the bare bones, no role, check or note; each part left out is taken in by its title with the notes it links, and taking every one gives every starter role (orchestrator, librarian, change-reviewer, explorer, story-author, frontend-builder, blind-reviewer, corpus-investigator), the six test-quality checks a review's brief lists, and the notes they stand on; the product holds no copy of its own, and joining it from another machine, or setting it up again after a failed try, adds none
6.8 · Setting a folder up as project "site" leaves a marker naming "site" and its database's identity, and the project's library exists

6.9 · Taking a newer starter pack adds what the library lacks and replaces only the pack records its user has not edited; an edited one is left and named with the newer text beside it; a product project holding no copy takes it into its factory

6.10 · A folder in no git repository gets one: makeRepository runs git init and commits the project's .storytree folder (its marker and .gitignore), says it made one, already had one, or could not (git missing); with no git identity it keeps the repository with that folder staged, and firstCommit makes that first commit once git has one, as it does for an older setup's root .storytree.json staged alone; it never fails the setup
6.11 · Setting a new project up finds the user's factory by its mark, or makes it, and names it, holding no copy of the starter pack; a join makes none
6.12 · Moving an existing project onto the user's factory drops its unedited copies the factory holds and keeps every record it edited or added

6.13 · Setting a folder up leaves its marker at .storytree/project.json, none at the root, and a .storytree/.gitignore holding *.local.json; a .gitignore the folder already has there is kept, the line added once and never doubled

capabilities.title: 12 · Import an existing project
capabilities.description: A storytree project imports an existing JavaScript or TypeScript project's folder (ADR-0993 D1, D2, D6): the folder is recorded on the project beside its trunk, with its repository and commit when it is a git checkout with a remote, and each package the folder declares (pnpm-workspace.yaml, else package.json workspaces, else the folder itself) becomes a mapped story through the library's mapStories, the only way a story is made mapped. Importing again maps the folder afresh, keeping what stands. The founding choice: the import reads the folder and writes nothing into it; the deliberate act of importing is its approval (ADR-0942). Front doors: storytree import <folder> and the import_project tool.

contracts.title: 12.1 · Importing a folder records it beside the project's trunk, with its repository and commit when it is a git checkout with a remote, and maps one story per package it declares, named as the package names itself, with no capabilities; nothing is written into the folder
12.2 · Importing a folder again adds a story for each new package, retires the stories whose package is gone, and leaves every other mapped story as it stands
12.3 · A folder that does not exist, is inside the storytree project, or has no package.json at its top is refused, saying why, and nothing is written

12.4 · Importing a folder again says the commit recorded before and the one recorded now, and the files added, changed and removed between them (nothing when git cannot compare them), and names each explored capability whose covered files are gone, leaving it as it stands
12.5 · A workspace pattern that climbs out of the folder or runs past the matching limits is refused, saying why, and nothing is written; any '*' pattern is matched in time linear in the folder name

capabilities.title: 6 · Pixel-art shorts
capabilities.description:
Short pixel-art video clips about storytree, rendered from code by Remotion in packages/website/src/shorts: each frame is drawn at low resolution (480×270) and scaled up ×4 with nearest-neighbour (ADR-1084 D1). Each is a side-by-side, without storytree on the left and with it on the right, in the same room, PixelLab's: the desk of the owner's 2026-10-18 reference, with a normal-size monitor, keyboard, mouse and mug, the developer's hands on the keyboard, and the room inpainted round it. What the screen shows is drawn behind the room and shows through its screen; a beat whose screen must be read cuts to a full view of it. Where a screen shows the map, it is the forest's own view drawing the glass sheet of the shop built with storytree, from the website's saved shop snapshot, shrunk into the short's palette; one frame component (short.tsx's MapShortFrame) mounts the view, aims it, gives it each moment's props and hands each frame to the short's scene.

The first short, "seeing what agents built" (56 s, polished against a written bar in increment_ea834305fe2d and again on the owner's notes in increment_fa48e88589f9): both developers ask Claude to build a shop in a brand-new project (re-cut in increment_baeb6376f044, ADR-1110): without storytree the reply says it is done; with it, the map grows from an empty glass sheet as Claude builds (the shop's saved growth replayed by the forest's own growth), the wishlist rising last as its new island, and clicking it opens the app's panel and its capability graph (the forest's drill-down laid out by layoutTree). The developer without storytree is never frustrated: he keeps reading the code. It plays on claim 1 of storytree.dev.

The second short, "one map for you and your agents" (58 s, increment_761f3f5755c8, ADR-1104 D2): both developers give two Claude Code sessions, side by side, the same two jobs. Without storytree the agents pile up large diffs in one checkout, and the second rewrites the file the developer is reviewing. With storytree he and both agents see one map: each session's claim stands on the shop's map as the forest's own flag (read from the view each frame and drawn as a pixel pennant in the session's colour, named by its part), the second agent is told the part it wanted is claimed and starts elsewhere, takes it once the first lets it go, and what he reviews is small. It plays on claim 2.

The third short, "memory that lives where your code lives" (54 s, increment_f474a8e4b7e7, ADR-1104 D2): both developers ask Claude Code to clean up checkout's total. Without storytree the agent's memory is not tied to the code, so it tidies away why tax is rounded once, on the total, cannot say why when asked, the memory file he scrolls has nothing on that file, and the bug fixed once before comes back. With storytree the agent reads the Checkout story, the code attached to it and the memory attached to it, before it edits, and keeps the reason; on the map the story is the Checkout island, lit by his click, its panel listing its code and its memory. It plays on claim 3.

The developer and the room come from PixelLab, assembled into a committed sprite sheet; the screens and a 3×5 screen font are drawn in code. Tests computed from the scripts and layouts pin reading times, length, fit, that no sprite covers a line to be read, the maps and their claims; rendered frames pin crisp pixels, determinism and the real view's flags. Each short's renders (a 1080p MP4 the site serves and social media can take, its poster and a still of each beat) are committed in its evidence folder (evidence/first-short, evidence/one-map, evidence/memory), beside the first short's polish loops.

stories.title: Mick's dev loop
stories.description: A session developing storytree gets the personal half of its dev loop from Mick's factory: the guidance build and check, the gate steps for plan edges, owner-applied folders and the risk line, the library tools, the lag instruments, the evidence sweep, the scripts that carry the repository to a new one, the coverage survey and test ratio, and the heavy-run lock storytree's pnpm test and pnpm gate hold. Its code is the micks-dev-loop plugin in HuaMick/storytree-factory (ADR-1192 D2, ADR-1174), moved there from storytree's packages/dev-loop, which is gone: it reaches storytree only through the checkout it runs in, is added as a part of its own (named in settings, standing in for none of storytree's), and its tests run in the factory, not in storytree's CI. The base half (the scoped test runner, the worktree installer, the merge-queue scripts) is the base dev loop's, and the repository's own checks are storytree's repo-checks.

capabilities.title: 8 · Lag instruments
capabilities.description: The kept instruments that measure the app's lag (ADR-0836, ADR-1001), so every lane and re-measure compares before and after with the same instrument and the same seed: `pnpm lag:reads` times the page's reads over a throwaway Postgres with added latency per query, and `pnpm lag:desktop` performs the catalogue of named actions (opening the smallest, largest and a named story's island, closing the panel, Library and back, opening a Library note and a session's row, a hover sweep, turning the map in the forest and the Library by a Ctrl+drag, idle) through real input on an instrumented copy of the desktop app, or the desktop page in headless Chromium over the stand-in bridge (`--chromium`, as on the Mint box), and prints each action's response, longest frame, settled time and IPC count against its budget, saying NOT RUN for any it could not perform. With `--against <ref | built app dir>` it measures this checkout's build and the other in alternating rounds on the same seed and says, per action, slower, the same or faster, with any read whose count differs as its own finding. The whole run queues behind the heavy-run lock. On the Mint box, `pnpm lag:box` runs it after merges rather than by hand (ADR-1001 D3): a systemd user timer every 15 minutes measures the newest main against each action's baseline, one bounded run at a time with the merges between skipped; a slowdown counts when a second run agrees, holds the baseline back, and is halved down to the pull request that caused it; the history sits in the storytree-lag database beside the library, which `pnpm lag:box` prints from any machine, and `pnpm lag:box rebaseline` accepts a cost with its reason. Never a gate: nothing of it runs in CI or a pull request's checks. They run from Mick's factory plugin micks-dev-loop (`storytree lag-instruments reads|desktop|box`, which the root scripts call), so only on a computer that names it; the box's timer starts the plugin's lag-box.mjs in its runner checkout.

capabilities.title: 8 · Code survey
capabilities.description: Surveys story source packages and app frame paths (apps/desktop/src) for file ownership, source line counts and imports. Retains tests with numbered N.M titles and import edges, separately tagged as tests and excluded from source line counts. Ownership follows existing nearest numbered-test reach, execution coverage and type-import rules (8.1, 8.6, 8.7); unmatched files remain unclaimed. Lives in packages/map under ADR-0864; the forest consumes this survey for drawing. Callers may survey the current checkout explicitly. The main default reads immutable Git blobs from fetched origin/main, with shared bounded asynchronous fetches, keeping the last fetched main offline and reporting failure when none exists. A start's reader (the desktop's) answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch (8.27). No checkout is changed. Without origin, the primary folder is surveyed; non-Git folders are read directly. Unchanged blob identities retain file and story surveys. The forest owns request pacing; each later request checks for the next landing, so no cooldown can swallow its only refresh.

contracts.title: 8.1 · A source file a test titled "N.M …" reaches belongs to capability N of that test's story, whether the test imports it directly or reaches it through any number of further ordinary imports and re-exports. When tests of several capabilities reach it, the capability whose tests reach it nearest (fewest ordinary imports away; a re-export adds none) owns it, then the one whose tests reach it that near most, then the lower number.

reported.note: 40806c36: all 19 Code survey proofs pass, plus foreground gate typecheck/12 affected units/plan edges. Historical actual alias replay 754/67597 to729/67597; same-base current alias replay756 to731. Relative import equivalents confirm existing allocation ranking.

contracts.title: 8.3 · A file's lines of code are counted for source files only: a test file, or a test helper under a testing/ folder, adds no lines to any file, capability or story.
8.4 · A relative import from one source file to another is reported as a link from the importing file to the imported one.

reported.note: Final PR #553 head 70c8bf8acf3ef16374ab897aa46505c9b3353bbf uses @babel/parser solely to identify real module syntax and comments, with parseable-prefix recovery for unfinished edits. 15 focused tests pass; final foreground full gate passed typecheck, all 17 units and plan edges; guidance NOT RUN (unchanged). Exact paired readCodeSurvey removes Website collision, 1801/67836 -> 1805/67886 project unclaimed/total; 4-line Map residue is increment_1680b681eaed. Earlier TypeScript dependency experiment was removed after bundling checks rejected it. CI and merge pending.

contracts.title: 8.5 · Surveying again reads no unchanged file (same path and Git blob in a merged snapshot, or size and modified time on disk), reads changed files again, and reuses an unchanged story survey.

8.6 · A source file a numbered test's runs executed, in its own process or one it started, belongs to the capability whose tests executed it most (the package's coverage map); a direct import outranks it, and it outranks a file reached only through further imports.

8.7 · A source file a numbered test reaches only through type imports (a file of types, or one imported only for its types) belongs to the capability whose tests reach it so nearest, then most; any reach by a value import or by running it outranks a reach by types.
8.8 · Each surveyed story names the stories whose packages its package depends on, through any dependency field of its package.json.
8.9 · The survey includes apps/desktop/src files under the app story, attributing their capabilities by the same numbered-test ownership rules as package source files.

8.10 · The survey retains test files tagged as tests, their N.M numbered test titles and their import edges, without adding them to source file, capability or story line counts. Number lists are validated before expansion: at most 256 entries per title and 4096 per surveyed test file, counting repeated entries before deduplication; invalid or over-budget titles supply no proof identities and do not stop other files from surveying.

Paired survey 825/67630 -> 825/67636; six added Map source lines allocated, no unclaimed reduction. Independent review checking 11 reweights of already-allocated Library/Agent-link files.

contracts.title: 8.11 · Selecting current surveys that checkout, including local changes. The main default surveys fetched origin/main without changing any checkout, follows subsequent landings, and shares bounded asynchronous Git work per repository. If origin is unavailable it retains the last fetched main; without one it reports failure, in words that name why (Git's own reason, such as an origin with no main or one that cannot be read, or the reason its fetch was skipped) and that tell the refusal apart by its message alone. A repository without origin, or a non-Git folder, keeps the primary-folder reading.

8.12 · A CommonJS `require` of a string naming a relative file, or the package's own exported subpath, is an ordinary import: a test reaches what it requires and everything that requires in turn, so a CommonJS package's files fall in the capabilities whose tests reach them

contracts.title: 8.13 · A numbered test outside the package’s src reaches its source as a test in src would; outside src the reader follows test files and their helper dependencies within the package, without counting their lines as source or reading unrelated scripts
8.14 · A test file that runs an imported behaviour suite carries the suite's numbered titles

contracts.title: 8.15 · A source file's opening "Capability N · <title>" declaration (after a shebang) puts it on capability N's territory when N's numbered tests or coverage map reach it; a declaration they do not reach, or an undeclared file, is allocated by inference
8.16 · A survey can be read on a worker thread: the same answer as reading it in place, while the asking thread's event loop stays free

8.17 · A changed file is placed in its capability by its own declaration, else by the survey's inference, flagged as inferred; a file in no story's package, or a file that cannot be read, is placed nowhere
8.18 · A source file's import of a name from another story's package is an edge from its capability to the capability of the file that defines the name, type-only when every import behind it is
8.19 · A derived edge whose file at either end has no capability is kept as a story-to-story edge, naming the files that cause it

8.20 · A mapped story is surveyed from the folder this machine imports it from: the JavaScript and TypeScript files tracked at its checkout's commit under its folders, leaving out the skip list's folders and a folder another package of the same import maps, each with its non-blank lines and no capability, read without parsing; a mapped story whose import this machine does not name is absent
8.21 · A mapped story's package dependency on another mapped story's package is a road between them; a loop among mapped stories is reported with the stories round it, and refuses nothing
8.22 · Surveying again while an imported checkout is at the same commit reads none of its files and keeps each mapped story's survey; at a new commit only the files whose blob changed are read
8.23 · A built story's package dependency on a mapped story's package is a road from it to the mapped story; a mapped story's dependency on a built story's package is never a road

8.24 · Work done at source in an imported checkout counts before it is committed there: a changed or new file Git does not ignore is read from disk over the commit's tree, a deleted one leaves, and only those files are read; while that work is unchanged a survey again reads none of them

8.25 · A start whose fetched main is the commit last surveyed, with the same plan, answers from the survey kept between starts without reading or parsing a file; another plan or a newer main is surveyed afresh and kept in its turn

8.26 · a mapped story's file under the folders or files an explored capability covers carries that capability, work not yet committed included; the rest carry none, and a change of covers is read at the same commit
8.27 · A start's reader answers its first ask from the main already fetched while it fetches, and its next ask waits on that fetch and surveys what it brought

8.28 · A '#' specifier the importing package's package.json imports field names literally is an ordinary import of the file it maps to, so a file reached only that way falls in the capability whose numbered test imports it

8.29 · A source file whose opening header's title is not the title of the capability its number names in its story (as a file moved from another story keeps) declares nothing: it is placed by the survey's inference, or nowhere, never in the capability its stale number names

8.30 · A story that owns several packages has each package's files surveyed under its capabilities, paths from the package named after its title, and its edit claims and tested numbers read from every one
8.31 · An edge file whose source file declares nothing of its own, imports nothing of its own package and passes on names from one other story's package is marked a forwarder
8.32 · A numbered test in any script extension's test file carries its contract's number
8.33 · Declared build steps and cleanups are marked on survey edges

8.34 · A test file's esbuild entry point, written as a literal new URL("./x", import.meta.url) inside an entryPoints array, is an ordinary import of the file it names, so a module a numbered test bundles for the browser falls in that test's capability

8.35 · The survey's Git runs no program its repository's settings name, and its fetch of main is skipped, with the reason, when those settings name an upload program, an ssh command or a credential helper

8.36 · A pytest test whose name is test_<n>_<m>_… or whose docstring starts <n>.<m>, in a test_*.py or *_test.py file anywhere in the checkout but Git's ignored files, carries that contract number for the landing check
8.37 · A pytest number prefixed with a story's package counts for that story only, and an unprefixed one counts for a story only while no other story plans a contract with that number

8.38 · Each path given, absolute or relative to the folder, is placed in its checkout: its story and that story's package, apps/desktop for the desktop app's, even for a file the survey does not read, and its capability when it declares one or the survey infers it; a path in no story's package is placed nowhere

8.39 · A bare specifier naming another package of the same story is an ordinary import of the file its exports map it to, so a test in one of a story's packages reaches the files of its other package it imports; another story's package stays unreached

capabilities.title: 4 · A factory plugin's own tests
