capabilities.title: 1 · Arm switch
capabilities.description: The arm record, and the verdict the doors ask for (ADR-1064 D2). An arm names its experiment, its name, the verbs it denies by door (tools by name, commands by family), and the guidance, role and review variants it swaps. A lane's storytree home names its experiment and arm in settings.json (Project and caller's Settings); this capability reads it and answers each verb allowed or denied-by-arm. The doors stay thin: they ask, refuse and log; the labels on every line are Session management's stamp of the same setting.

contracts.title: 1.1 · A verb's verdict is read from the caller's storytree home: a home whose settings name no experiment allows every verb; a home naming an arm gets denied-by-arm, with the experiment and arm, for each tool and command family its settings say that arm denies, and nothing else; no arm is held in code.
1.2 · A home naming an arm but not what it denies is refused, naming the arm and saying that its run carries the denies, so a lane started outside its run never runs as if unswitched.
1.3 · An arm's denies are carried into the home that names it, its other settings kept; a home naming no arm, or another, is refused and nothing is written.
1.4 · Experiments contributes its arm check to the doors through its manifest

capabilities.title: 2 · Arm workspaces
capabilities.description: A throwaway library and storytree home per arm (ADR-1064 D3): a database and role named x-<experiment>-<arm> on the box's cluster, made and dropped the way tests make theirs, and a home whose settings point at it and name the arm. Never the real storytree project.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Making an arm gives it a role and a database named for it and a home pointing there, whose key opens the arm's own project, and never touches the real project
2.2 · Dropping an arm drops its database, role and home, and leaves the real library's records and every other arm as they were
2.3 · An experiment or arm name that is not lower-case words and hyphens, or one too long, is refused before anything is made; a home naming another arm is never removed

2.4 · Experiments declares `experiment arm make`, `grant` and `drop`, which act on the cluster holding the caller's library on this machine and are refused, making nothing, where the library is not there
2.5 · An arm's role reads and adds to the server's shared activity and QA databases and reads its routing and points, never deleting there; granted by make, again by grant, revoked by drop
2.6 · The arm verbs sign in to the cluster as this machine's own user over its local socket, with no password, never as the library's role

capabilities.title: 3 · Arm repositories
capabilities.description: A public throwaway repository per arm in the storytree-ai organisation (ADR-1064 D3, as the owner amended it 2026-10-16), seeded from the task, with Linux-only CI, the merge queue on, and the task's verifier as a job; archived when the experiment ends. The task's hidden tests are never committed: CI fetches them at run time with a secret the lanes do not hold. Creating these repositories is approved by the owner's answer on question_b8a73d781784.

contracts.title: 3.1 · An arm's CI runs on Linux only: its own checks gate every pull request and merge-queue entry, and the task's hidden tests run only on each merge to main, fetched with a secret, out of the reach of the arm's code, reporting counts alone
3.2 · Making an arm's repository creates it public in storytree-ai, seeded from the starting tree with the arm's CI, sets its secrets through stdin, and turns the merge queue on for main
3.3 · Ending an experiment archives each of its arms' repositories

3.4 · An arm's workflow, which runs the hidden tests with their token after each merge, changes only with a code owner's review, and its one code owner is the identity its lanes act as, so no lane can approve its own change

capabilities.title: 4 · Experiment record and freeze
capabilities.description: The experiment record, a new library kind (ADR-1064 D5): arms, hypotheses, measures, what counts as the variable helping, not helping or inconclusive, budget and stop rules. Freezing stamps the time and makes hypotheses and criteria read-only, so the reading can only add an outcome; `experiment run` refuses an unfrozen record.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Freezing an experiment stamps the time once, and a run reads only a frozen one

capabilities.title: 5 · Per-merge points and curves
capabilities.description: One point per merge and the curves they make (ADR-1064 D4): each merge on an arm's repository writes an experiment_points row (experiment, arm, merge number, pull request, time, verifier passed and total, tokens to date, collisions to date, file growth, imports crossing capability lines, rework), and `storytree experiment curves <experiment> [--json]` prints them as a series per arm. Per-lane measures are read from labelled activity lines, the QA ledger and transcript records.

contracts.title: 5.1 · Recording an arm writes one point per merge to main, in merge order, with its hidden-tests counts and the tree's files and bytes, never twice, stopping at a merge whose run has not finished
5.2 · A merge whose arm workflow differs from the one it was seeded with is recorded as changed, and its curve flags it
5.3 · experiment curves prints each arm's points as a series, and --json gives them as data per arm
5.4 · Each point carries the tokens the arm's sessions had spent by its merge, read from the arm's own project's stored transcripts, and the curves give them
5.5 · Each point carries the arm's collisions by its merge: claims refused, pull requests gone red and, of those, conflicts with main, from the arm's own project's lines
5.6 · Each point carries its rework: the lines its merge removed that one of the five merges before it added, matched by file and text, a blank line or an older merge's never counted
5.7 · each point carries the imports crossing capability lines in the arm's tree at its merge, and the source lines they are counted over
5.8 · The seed the import pushed is point zero, with the counts its push's hidden-tests run printed against the untouched start, recorded once and before any merge, and the curves show it as the seed
5.9 · An arm recorded without the CI it was seeded with judges each merge's workflow against the one at its seed commit, still after the seed is recorded, and refuses when it has no seed to judge by
5.10 · Recording an experiment records each of its arms in turn, an arm that fails said without stopping the others, and says per arm what it wrote and where it waits
5.11 · Curves read a run's points by its record's id or its short name

capabilities.title: 6 · Stop rules
capabilities.description: Stop rules (ADR-1064 D6): an arm stops when the verifier's share has not risen for the number of merges its frozen record names, or at the record's wall-clock limit; every arm pauses, never stops, while the real pool has ranked work waiting. Tokens are recorded as a measure, never a cap.

contracts.title: 6.1 · The stop rules are read from the frozen record's words; a record naming no flat-curve merges or wall-clock limit is refused
6.2 · An arm stops once its verifier share has not risen for the record's number of merges, and never before
6.3 · An arm stops at the wall-clock limit from its first dispatched lane, and once its verifier passes every test

capabilities.title: 7 · Experiment dispatcher
capabilities.description: The experiment dispatcher, `storytree experiment run <experiment> --as <name> --rules <file>` (ADR-1064 D3): it feeds lanes only from its arms' throwaway libraries, shares the box's lane count, takes a slot only when the real pool has no ranked work waiting and one slot stays free for real work, and alternates arms (fewer lanes first, kept across restarts). It reaches the agent pool by running its files as processes, never by package import (settled by increment_0a8db531dffe): `packages/agent-pool/src/launch.mjs ready [project]` reads what the real pool, or an arm's library through the arm's home, would start now, with the engines running and the cap; `runner.mjs run` runs each arm lane in the arm's checkout with the arm's home as STORYTREE_HOME. The command line and the MCP server import this package, so an import would have given both doors a path into the dev loop's story.

contracts.title: 7.1 · A run carries each arm's denies from the frozen record into the arm's home, none when the record names none; an arm whose home is not its own, or has no checkout, refuses the run before any home is written
7.2 · It takes a slot only while the real pool has no ranked work waiting, leaving one slot for real work; ranked work pauses it, never stops it
7.3 · It alternates the arms, fewer lanes first across restarts, and never starts an increment twice or again within the back-off
7.4 · An arm whose stop rule holds is stopped and kept stopped while the other runs on; the run ends when every arm has stopped
7.5 · Each arm lane is the agent pool's lane runner, run as its own process in the arm's checkout with the arm's home as its storytree home
7.6 · `experiment run` refuses, at the door, an unfrozen record and a frozen one whose stop rules it cannot read
7.7 · Each look records the arms' new merges as points before their stop rules read the curves, saying what it recorded; a record that fails is said and the look goes on
7.8 · An arm with nothing ready is given one planning lane for its first arc whose state it has not planned in, never two at once, kept across restarts and counted among its lanes

7.9 · A build lane's brief names its increment and ends with the lane rules; a planning lane's names its arc and ends with the planning rules beside the dispatcher; each names the arm's home, library and checkout

7.10 · A run approves each arm's checkout as its trunk, as the machine its home names, through the admin's connection: one with no trunk is recorded approved, one recorded unapproved is approved, one already approved is left alone, and a project whose trunk is elsewhere refuses the run
7.11 · A planning lane that ends with its arm's arc unchanged and nothing ready leaves that arc offered again after the back-off, said once; one after which work is ready leaves it planned
7.12 · A run restarted while an unchanged arc waits out its back-off keeps the back-off: the arc is offered again only once it has passed
7.13 · An arc that returns to an arm's plannable list is offered again
7.14 · An arm whose planning changes nothing three times running stops as declared done
7.15 · An arm lane's folders never list the run's scores or another arm's reviews
7.16 · A look runs the agent runner's exported launch entry as its own process, as the arm's home when it is an arm's

capabilities.title: 8 · Harbor task adapter
capabilities.description: The Harbor task adapter, `storytree experiment task import <harbor-task-dir>` (ADR-1064 D7): it reads task.toml, instruction.md, environment/ and tests/, seeds each arm's repository from the starting tree, parks the instruction as each arm's one arc in its throwaway library, and writes the verifier into CI as a job that builds the task's image, fetches the hidden tests, runs them against the merged tree and reports per-test results.

8.2 · The verifier counts what a Harbor verifier left: a CTRF report's tests, a metrics file's passed and total, or a reward as one test; a run that stopped before its tests is none of the task's total, or no result when that is not known; nothing left is a failure

8.5 · The instruction is parked as the one arc in the arm's own throwaway library, opened through the arm's home; a library that has an arc already refuses another

8.6 · Experiments declares `experiment task import`, which reads the two tokens CI holds as saved keys and is refused, naming each unsaved key and making nothing, until both are saved; with no arms named it imports into the arms made for the experiment in this storytree home

stories.title: Agent runner
stories.description: Ready work is turned into landed pull requests without a person at the keyboard: a dispatcher picks ready increments from the library and starts lanes under a machine's cap and pace, each lane runs on the engine its allowance allows, and a watcher lands each handed-over pull request, starting a fix session on a red. Its Claude Code mod rides in every Claude Code session given its plugin folder, the runner's lanes and interactive sessions alike, and hands the session's hook events, heartbeat and live usage to storytree through the session's own tool server, with no process started for them (ADR-1076 D5). It works without the dev loop, and the dev loop works without it (ADR-1071 D3). Its code lives in packages/agent-pool, the mod in src/claude-code-mod; the repo root's agent-pool.json is the owner's configuration of it (the Mint box), and packages/dev-loop/src/lanes keeps forwarders at the old paths the box's live processes run.

capabilities.title: 4 · A watcher lands a handed-over pull request
capabilities.description: A session on any machine ends once its pull request is open and its gate is green, and hands the PR to a watcher with no model (packages/dev-loop/src/lanes/watch.mjs): `watch.mjs handover <pr> <increment>` runs `hand` on the box directly, or over `ssh mint` from another machine with the session's own id, refusing with the reason when the box is out of reach (ADR-0974). `hand` records the hand-off in ~/storytree-lanes/watch/, sets an event wait on the increment so no other session takes it while it lands, and starts the watcher if none runs. The watcher polls GitHub: on MERGED it clears the wait, closes the increment landed with the PR and releases the session's remaining claims; on a red (a failed check, a conflict with main, or an ejection from the merge queue) it clears the wait and starts one fix session for that PR, which fixes, pushes and hands back; after its fix limit it writes an owner wait with the PR and the logs. A conflict with main reads as one whatever else failed (13.18), gets one more fix session (13.12), and past that never waits on the owner: the hand-off is dropped and the increment goes back on its arc as ready work, its body naming the PR and its branch (13.20). A fix session whose branch moved while it ran is not counted when the next red is a conflict, and a cap on all sessions per PR (WATCH_FIX_CAP, 6) stops a loop (13.19). A fix session refused by another session's claim hands back with --refused and counts for nothing (13.14), and conflicts with main are merged by one fix session at a time, lowest pull request first (13.15). The watcher also owns a stopped release (ADR-1032 D2): every five minutes its look loop reads the latest published release, the release runs and main's CI runs from GitHub; a release attempt or main's newest CI run that failed is rerun once (main's, and a handed-over pull request's red, again up to a run's fourth attempt while every failed job is the runner's: no runner took it, or the browser crashed at launch, 4.29), and a stop that outlasts the rerun (main still red, the last two release attempts failed, or a commit green on main for over two hours in no published release) starts one fix session at a time, none while one lives or its pull request or question is open, and past the fix limit asks the owner on the release arc (arc_312aa103bfca) (13.16, 13.17). The watcher (`run`) is a keeper over its look loop (`watch`), which exits with the restart code once the dev loop's code in the shared checkout changes, so the keeper starts it again on the new code; `status` says when the running look loop's code differs from the checkout's, or predates the version it records (13.21). It is not an engine, so it counts against no engine slot; its fix sessions are. Founded on decision_e101df427118 (ADR-0955 D3). Every hour the look loop also reads main's first-parent history of the owner's secret-check exemptions list (.github/secret-check-exemptions.txt) from git and records one FYI per commit that changed the paths it exempts: what it added and took away, the pull request and who opened it; each FYI is about `<list>@<sha>`, which the library is asked for first, so a change is told once and none is missed between looks (4.42, increment_67dc251f5856: awareness, not prevention, question_82ab3da6eb69). The watcher and the sessions it starts run in freeOf's environment, without the handing-over session's id or its lane's run marker, so the lane runner does not stop them when that lane ends (4.43).

stories.title: Keys
stories.description: A user gives storytree a key once and every storytree process (the app, the command line, the MCP server) finds it: saved with `storytree auth set` into an auth.json in storytree's home that only the user can read, or pointed at the user's own store with a `!<command>` entry, with the vendor's environment variable as the fallback. storytree borrows a login the user already has wherever one exists and keeps a key only when nothing can be borrowed (ADR-0843). The library (a library reached by address finds its password here) and Experiments (arm workspaces and Harbor tasks) call it, and it calls no other story. Its code lives in packages/keys (ADR-1075, which took it back out of The library; the earlier Keys story, story_55eb820f95c9, was folded by ADR-1066).

radius.reason: 23 packages downstream; public users, inherited from packages/website

capabilities.title: 1 · Key store and resolver
capabilities.description: Keeps the keys storytree must hold in one auth.json in storytree's home, only the user can read and write it, and many processes can write it at once safely. It resolves a named key the same way in every process: an explicit value, then the file entry (a literal, or a `!<command>` run once per process), then the environment variable. `storytree auth set|list|remove` is its command-line front door: the cli family parses, calls this package and prints.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Saving a key creates `auth.json` in storytree's home (`STORYTREE_HOME` when set, else `~/.storytree/0.3`, the folder `settings.json` uses), readable and writable by the user alone: on macOS and Linux the file's mode is 0600; on Windows it relies on the user-profile folder's own permissions, and nothing changes them.

1.2 · Two writers saving different keys at once both survive: reading `auth.json` back after they finish finds both entries, because every write holds a file lock and writes a temporary file that is then renamed over `auth.json`, so a reader never sees a half-written file.

1.3 · Resolving a key returns, first to last, an explicit value given by the caller, then its `auth.json` entry, then its environment variable: with all three present the explicit value wins; with no explicit value a saved entry wins over the environment variable; with neither, the environment variable is returned; with none, resolving says the key is not set.

1.4 · An `auth.json` entry `!<command>` resolves to the command's standard output, trimmed, and resolving it again in the same process does not run the command again; a command that fails is an error naming the key and that its command failed, which never contains the command's output.

1.5 · `storytree auth set <name>` reads the value from standard input, takes none as an argument and never prints it; `storytree auth list` prints each key's name and where it resolves from (file, command or environment) and never a value; `storytree auth remove <name>` deletes that entry from `auth.json`, leaving the others.

stories.title: The local database
stories.description: storytree runs a Postgres of its own on this computer, from binaries it ships, so a user installs nothing: it finds the Postgres tools for the machine (or the ones a packaged app ships), makes a cluster on a data directory and starts one server on it, refuses a second start while a live process holds that directory and clears what a dead one left behind, signs every client in with the installation's password as an ordinary role, and drops the throwaway databases tests make. Setup (the developer database and home a project connects to) and the dev loop (the test server, the guidance build, the library server and the lag readings) call it; the desktop app starts its server through it, and The library's tests make their databases on it. It calls no other story. Its code lives in packages/local-postgres (ADR-1076 D1, which took it back out of The library; the earlier story, story_1d360b6227d8, was folded by ADR-1066).

capabilities.title: 2 · A server on a data directory
capabilities.description: Makes a cluster in a data directory the first time, asking every connection for the installation's password (SCRAM; a legacy trust cluster is converted at start), starts a server on it listening on 127.0.0.1 only, makes sure clients' ordinary role (storytree: may create databases, owns every database, no superuser) exists and owns what the superuser made before, hands back its url signing in as that role, and publishes the private connection handoff (ADR-0941) while it runs; stops it; while it runs, an owner record beside the directory (`<dataDir>.owner.json`) names the process that holds it, which is how others learn whether storytree is running and where.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A cluster is made only where there is none, asking every connection for the installation's password and listening on 127.0.0.1 only; a directory holding anything else is refused and left untouched.
2.2 · A started server answers SELECT 1 at the url handed back; stop stops it, a second stop is harmless, and it can be started again, on a port asked for.
2.3 · A start on a data directory a live process holds is refused with a DataDirInUseError naming that process and its owner, and the holder's server is left running.
2.4 · A server left running by a process that died is stopped and replaced, and a dead owner's record alone is cleared, so the start goes ahead.

2.5 · A start can carry server settings for that run, as the throwaway test server runs with fsync, synchronous commit and full-page writes off; a start without them keeps the cluster's own, and a setting that is not one plain word is refused before anything starts.

2.9 · A throwaway test server can hand back the superuser's url beside its client's, for tests' setup, while its clients and handoff stay the ordinary role

stories.title: Test waits
stories.description: A developer's test waits for what it needs (a server up, a child gone, a file written) and removes its temp folders through one helper that backs off inside a budget scaled by how slow the machine running it is, so a test tuned on Linux holds on CI's slower Windows runners (ADR-1156).

depth.reason: no depth flag in its code

radius.reason: 25 packages downstream; public users, inherited from packages/website

capabilities.title: 1 · The environment's factor
capabilities.description: How much slower than Linux the machine running the tests is, read from one place, so no test carries its own platform guess (ADR-1156 D2).

contracts.title: 1.1 · The factor is 1 on Linux and larger on Windows and macOS

capabilities.title: 2 · Waiting for a check
capabilities.description: A test states what it waits for and a budget in its own terms; the helper retries with exponential backoff until the check holds or the scaled budget is spent, then fails naming what and how long. Its companion watches a scaled window for something that must not happen (ADR-1156 D1).

contracts.title: 2.1 · A wait backs off and ends within its scaled budget
2.2 · A wait that runs out fails naming what it waited for and how long
2.3 · A quiet check watches the whole scaled window

capabilities.title: 3 · Removing a test's folders
capabilities.description: A test's temp folder or file is removed through one helper that retries while Windows still holds it (EBUSY, EPERM, ENOTEMPTY, EACCES), within a budget scaled by the environment's factor (ADR-1156 D3).

contracts.title: 3.1 · A removal retries while the folder is held
3.2 · A folder still held past the scaled budget is left with a warning

stories.title: Base dev loop
stories.description: A developer gets from a change to a landing check with one command: the gate runs the project's typecheck and tests, then every step the project's parts contribute, and ends in a PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN table with a reason for every row that did not pass. It runs in a user's project as in storytree's own; its code lives in packages/base-dev-loop.

radius.reason: 1 package downstream; no audience of its own or downstream, so owner

capabilities.title: 2 · Test scoping
capabilities.description: Decides from a branch's changes which packages `pnpm test` runs, the same way locally and in CI, and says so on its first line (`scope: ...`); flags force everything, name units, or rerun what failed (test-scope.mjs). Moved from Mick's dev loop to the base dev loop by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1192 D1), where it was 1.

contracts.title: 2.1 · A change inside a package runs that package and every package that depends on it, and no other.

2.2 · A change the workspace graph cannot account for (a root file, a package.json, the lockfile, the dev loop's own package) or an unreadable origin/main runs everything, and the first line says why.
2.3 · `--full` runs everything, `--only` runs the named units, and `--rerun-failed` reruns only what failed or never ran.
2.5 · A file named to run alone is a unit of its own whenever its package runs, and its package's unit runs every other file

capabilities.title: 3 · Worktree setup
capabilities.description: Installs a fresh or stale worktree when a session starts, so a session can build at once, and keeps the owner's local app following merged main (provision-worktree.mjs). Moved from Mick's dev loop to the base dev loop by increment_fc3a008fe1c6 (ADR-1192 D1), where it was 2.

contracts.title: 3.1 · A worktree that is installed and current is left alone, and as a session-start hook the check exits 0 and prints nothing.
3.2 · A fresh, stale or unlinked worktree gets `pnpm install`.

reported.note: Targeted provisioning tests pass 9/9. Root workspace dependencies are checked; missing links take precedence over a stale installed lockfile; --check refuses with the repair command and session-start provisioning reinstalls. Full gate running.

contracts.title: 3.3 · A failed install is retried once; failing again, the agent is told which condition failed and where to run `pnpm install`.

3.4 · A primary checkout on main behind locally fetched origin/main names its commit gap and update command at session start, and cannot start the agent-link server; linked worktrees and other branches are left alone.

reported.note: All 12 provisioning tests pass, including stale-primary refusal and repair, preserving dirty/diverged work, and leaving feature branches and linked main worktrees alone.

contracts.title: 3.5 · An installed worktree whose Electron has no binary gets it fetched by Electron's own installer; a fetch that fails never fails the session

3.6 · The install skips onnxruntime's download in every environment unless the environment names its own choice, and in a Claude Code cloud container a container holding the route's Access token but no library setting is given the library's HTTPS address and joins its checkout, its committed marker kept and the .storytree files joining wrote taken away
3.7 · a worktree gets the push check as the pre-push hook its repository's worktrees share, leaving someone else's pre-push hook as it was

capabilities.title: 4 · Running the tests
capabilities.description: `pnpm test` runs the scoped units against a throwaway local Postgres, each unit under a deadline, reporting which test is still running, and ends in a PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN table; it holds whatever lock its caller hands it past the scope decision (storytree's own run hands it the heavy-run lock, Mick's dev loop's 6), a Node.js known to crash is refused at the start, and each run's reds are kept for the change-reviewer (test.mjs, unit-run.mjs, unit-pool.mjs, test-running-reporter.mjs, test-leftovers.mjs, server-log.mjs, red-runs.mjs, node-runtime.mjs, junit.mjs). contracts.title: 4.1 · A unit past its deadline is killed with its whole process tree, naming the test still running; completed failures print their assertion details and location before the deadline can kill the unit; a test that fails while leaving a handle open ends its unit with that failure, not a hang. A run given a deadline (STORYTREE_TEST_DEADLINE) cuts the unit running at it the same way and leaves later units NOT RUN; stalled outside any unit past it, the run names where it stalled and exits non-zero.

4.18 · The urls a run hands its tests for the Postgres it started name a 30-second connect_timeout, so a loaded machine's slow handshake fails no test

) runs only the matching tests
4.20 · A unit's end stops every Postgres server running on a data folder in its temp folder, whether it passed, failed or was killed, before the folder is removed

stories.title: Service host
stories.description: One long-running process per machine runs the long-running services that storytree's mounted parts declare: the built-in part while it is on, the factory plugin standing in for it while it is off. It runs only the services this machine's settings turn on, restarts them with back-off, marks one failed when it keeps ending, and says how each stands with `storytree services`. Its code is packages/service-host.

capabilities.title: 1 · Running services
capabilities.description: Which services this machine hosts (each declared service of each mounted part, turned on in this machine's settings), each run as its own child process with its output in the host's log under its name; always-services restarted with back-off and marked failed when they keep ending, every-services run on their cadence without overlap, and stopping by signal then kill.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The host runs each declared service of each mounted part that this machine's settings turn on, each as its own child process, and writes each line it prints to the host's log after the service's name; a service not turned on, or of a part not mounted, is not started
1.2 · An always service that ends is started again after 10 seconds, the wait doubling with each end up to 5 minutes; five ends within 10 minutes mark it failed, and it is not started again
1.3 · An every service is started on its cadence, and never while its last run still goes
1.4 · Stopping the host sends each running service the stop signal, which fires its host.stopping, and kills one still running 30 seconds later

capabilities.title: 2 · Listing and restarting services
capabilities.description: `storytree services` lists every declared service on this machine: on or off, running, failed with its last lines, or waiting, and the factory commit the host last ran; `storytree services restart <part>/<service>` starts a failed one again; `storytree services run` runs the host in the foreground.

2.3 · storytree services run runs the service host in the foreground until a stop signal (Ctrl-C or SIGTERM) or a stop request (on Windows, where no signal is heard), then stops every service it ran and says so

2.4 · storytree services says when a part switch has not taken in the running host: a service turned on that the host did not mount at its start, or one it still runs whose part is now off, takes at the host's next start, and it names the restart

capabilities.title: 3 · Keeping the host running
capabilities.description: `storytree services install` writes this machine's one entry point that keeps the service host running, and `storytree services uninstall` removes it: on Linux the systemd user unit storytree-host.service (Restart=always), enabled and started; on Windows the scheduled task storytree-host, at this user's logon, whose script starts the host again after any end but a clean one. Installing again is idempotent.

3.3 · The laptop's storytree-host task runs node itself on `storytree services run` in storytree's checkout at the user's logon, windowless and with no time limit, starting it again after any end but a clean one

3.4 · storytree services install writes the script and registers the task, again idempotently, stopping a running host cleanly before a change; services uninstall stops the host, deletes the task and removes its files

capabilities.title: 4 · Keeping the factory current
capabilities.description: On a cadence (15 minutes) the host fast-forwards this machine's factory clone to origin/main, reinstalling only on a lockfile change and putting HEAD back on a failed install; it updates only a clone on main with a clean tree, otherwise says not updated with why; after a move it restarts only the services whose plugin folder or manifest changed, re-reading their declarations; and it exits 3 when its own code (the storytree checkout) moves (ADR-1180 D3).

contracts.title: 4.1 · The host fast-forwards this machine's factory clone to origin/main on its cadence (15 minutes) and reinstalls only when the lockfile changed; a failed install puts HEAD back where it was, leaves the running services on their code, and says why

arcs.description:
Owner request, 8 October 2026: "setup an arc to fix the issues." This is the scoped remediation of the local Mint review, not a general security backlog or authorization to change running infrastructure.

Baseline: commit 08124e6286ff09843500a35120a38a685806a646. The review ran Codex gpt-6-astra with the existing ChatGPT login and xhigh reasoning. It finished 7 October 2026 at 23:26 Sydney time with five confirmed entries representing four distinct issues, 15 unverified entries, and zero conclusively rejected entries. desktop-install-001 and storage-library-001 are the same local PostgreSQL authentication issue. These are findings at the pinned source commit; re-check current main before writing code.

Authoritative evidence remains local:
- Windows: C:/code/storytree-security-reviews/20261007-mint-08124e62/report.json and report.txt; jobs/ contains independent verdicts and preserved test scripts/results.
- Mint: /home/mickh/storytree-security-reviews/20261007-mint-08124e62/ with the same report and jobs; source/ is the immutable review snapshot; manifest.json records hashes.
Source integrity passed. The local PostgreSQL issue was established statically; the other confirmed classes have bounded isolated probes plus source-traced downstream effects. No live installation was attacked, and no fixes have yet been applied by this planning session.

Independent challenge rule: verify attacker-controlled input, actual reachability, the crossed trust boundary and concrete impact. Confirmation requires two independent reviewers with traceable source/test evidence; disagreement, absent reviewers and missing context remain unverified. The report mechanically downgraded desktop-install-002 and -003 despite two confirming reviewers, because citation/proof validation was incomplete; resolve that evidence mismatch early.

Three jobs stopped with Codex's explicit cybersecurity-safeguard error: discover-agent-command, challenge-identity-secrets-b, challenge-delivery-infra-b. Their failure logs are evidence of missing coverage, not counterevidence against a finding. Use permitted source review and synthetic regression work; never bypass a safeguard or switch provider to evade it. If supported access or an owner decision is genuinely required, write the precise owner action/question on this arc and hold only that residue.

Execution limits: local source fixes and disposable network-isolated tests with synthetic records and credentials only. No GCP, real credentials in tests, live target services, deployments, production data changes, or changes to the owner's running database/configuration. Implement and test migration logic using disposable fixtures; applying it to a live installation needs separate authorization. Normal repository gate and CI/merge ceremony still apply to code landings. Mint dispatches use Codex gpt-6-astra on the existing ChatGPT login and preserve xhigh reasoning; no automatic provider fallback.

Priority: authenticate the local database first. The routing fix shares agent-link project-routing ownership with authentication integration, so coordinate claims; the cache and bounded-survey fixes are independent. The map fix references increment_4be9cef055f9 ("A code survey never stalls the main process") on arc_4d5ae4174a9c, but adds a specific security input bound and does not duplicate its broader performance investigation. The final verification increment waits for the four fixes and the two review/triage increments; add any newly confirmed fix as a dependency before closing verification.

arcs.description: Successor to the closed arc_0ab31fd59c88 ("The shared library costs little to read"), which fixed the 25 GB/hour whole-log bug (ADR-0927) but left a steady state well above its own 0.5 GB/hour target. Measured 2026-10-19 on the Mint library: Mint to laptop over Tailscale averaged about 27 GB/day since boot (64 GB in 57.5 h), about 1.2 GB/hour, nearly all Postgres; a 60 s sample was 20.6 MB/min to the laptop across 54 short-lived connections. At Cloud SQL's US$0.19/GB that is about US$150/month for the laptop alone. Biggest single reader seen: the pool dispatcher (launch.mjs) reading whole records by type with their bodies (SELECT id, type, version, fields ... FROM record WHERE type = $1), about 6.5 MB in 90 s. Each short-lived storytree CLI or hook process opens about four connections and re-reads from cold. Free today on the Mint box (ADR-0928); it matters only if the library returns to a metered cloud provider.
